quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Merge.
Upcoming change in direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: A red, eight-sided sign means stop.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 30 minutes of rain. Water mixes with oil and chemicals on the road that have not yet washed away. Drive with extra caution on slippery roads.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and step on the brake firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle cuts in front of you, take your foot off the gas. This creates space between you and the other vehicle without needing to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: The best way to avoid danger while driving is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Be aware of everything around your vehicle. Watch the front, sides, and rear. This helps you see problems early so you can change speed or position safely.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended if you drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Zero alcohol is allowed for drivers under 21. Any trace of alcohol in your system results in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street if:

options.text: You increase your speed before the turn.
Traffic on the street moves to the right.
Traffic on the street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic on the street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves left. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves right.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic, match the speed, signal, and then:

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in, since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap, match traffic speed, signal, and merge when safe. Do not expect other drivers to clear the lane for you. Stay alert to other traffic.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, check traffic by:

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using your rearview mirror.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic before entering a freeway.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.
Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: Look left and right to check for people or traffic crossing your path or entering from other directions.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not entered it yet. You should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it quickly.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as well. Keep extra distance between your car and the one in front of you. This gives you more time to stop if the other car stops suddenly. Use your headlights properly. Do not always use high beams.

questions.question: If you approach a flashing red traffic light, you:

options.text: Are traveling in the wrong direction.
Must treat it like a stop sign.
Cannot go until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light the same way you treat a stop sign. Come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. Let all other traffic and pedestrians go first before you proceed.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Slow down when the road is wet.
The road ahead has many turns or curves.
There will be more traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when wet. Reduce your speed when you see this sign.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should:

options.text: Turn into any lane.
Turn into the first lane.
Turn into the second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the first lane.
questions.explanation: When you turn, use the lane closest to where you are turning from and turn into the first available lane. When turning from a two-way street to a one-way street, turn into the first lane.

questions.question: Make room for cars entering the freeway by:

options.text: Slowing down.
Moving to a different lane.
Keeping your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moving to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Help cars entering the freeway by moving to another lane if you can. This creates space for them to merge safely. If you cannot move lanes, slow down to let them enter smoothly and safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Four lanes of traffic ahead.
A divided highway ahead.
Traffic going both ways ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic going both ways ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions coming up. This sign warns you that you are leaving a one-way road and will soon drive on a road with traffic going both ways.

questions.question: If cars keep passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than the traffic flow on an interstate, use the right lane.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until all vehicles are gone before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or lights, the vehicle to your right has the right-of-way. Let that vehicle go first. Then proceed in the order that vehicles arrived.

questions.question: You must let an emergency vehicle with siren and lights pass by:

options.text: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
Moving to the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.
Stopping right away, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with its siren and lights on, drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. Move again after the emergency vehicle has passed.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: On cold, wet days, shaded parts of the road freeze first and thaw last. These areas are more likely to be icy and slippery.

questions.question: If another car is passing you in a no passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down and let the other driver return to your lane safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the other driver return to your lane safely.
questions.explanation: Passing zones are marked based on how far drivers can see ahead. Let the passing vehicle return to your lane easily. This helps everyone avoid dangers ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the hill ahead.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you about a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed. Protect your brakes from overheating.

questions.question: If your wheels go off the road edge, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then slowly return to the road.
Turn back onto the road right away.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then slowly return to the road.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road immediately. Slow down, check traffic, and turn back onto the road only when it is safe.

questions.question: When should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often, to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a car is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often, to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Do not stare at one spot while driving. Check your rearview mirrors often so you know where cars near you are.

questions.question: On an interstate, what is the best way to avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on your right?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: Watch for on-ramps ahead on interstate highways. When you can, move left out of the right lane. This lets cars enter from the on-ramps on your right.
